newsitem.title: USA: Oakley sees flat margins in 96 2nd half.
newsitem.headline: Oakley sees flat margins in 96 2nd half.

text.p: Oakley Inc Chief Financial officer Link Newcomb said the company's margins are expected to remain flat but stable during the second half as general and administrative costs offset leverage from its launch of its new line of X Metal sunglasses.
"Overall, it will probably be fairly flat," he said of the margins. In the first half of 1996, gross profit fell to 70.6 percent of net sales from 72.1 percent a year earlier.
Analysts expect gross margins to remain slightly above 70 percent through 1997 with the X Metal glasses to be introduced in the fourth quarter providing improved margins.
In the first half of 1996, general and administrative expenses slid to 6.5 percent of net sales from 6.9 percent as the company spread its expenses over higher sales.
Newcomb spoke after making a presentation at the Montgomery Securities investment conference.
